mainTopic: Does a woman's regular cycle (וסת) still worry us when its day falls during her ימי זיבה? רב פפא tries to prove it from a משנה, using שמואל's explanation, and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע pushes back.
overview: רב פפא wants to prove that we still worry about a woman's usual day of bleeding even when that day falls in her ימי זיבה. He uses שמואל's reading of the משנה. A woman who usually sees on day 22 shifted to day 27, and the משנה forbids both days, even though her old day now lands in ימי זיבה. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע pushes back. Maybe the 22 days should be counted from day 27, and then the day lands in her ימי נדה, so there is no proof. He supports this with a chicken: when a broken routine starts again, it restarts from the latest event. רב פפא answers with the מחלוקת between ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן about fixing a וסת during ימי נדה. He argues that רבי יוחנן's case shows we count from a usual day even when she did not see on it. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע explains רבי יוחנן's case differently: the 1st, the 1st, the 25th, and the 1st again, where the 25th is just extra blood. רבין and the נחותי ימא reported רבי יוחנן his way, and the פרק בנות כותים ends.

steps.title: שמואל explains how the משנה counts the days
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the משנה's 'day 15' is counted from her טבילה, which equals day 22 from her last sighting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The משנה is only talking about a woman who sees on day 15 after her immersion, which is day 22 after her last sighting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings שמואל's explanation of the משנה. רב פפא will use it as the basis for his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה speaks of a woman used to seeing on day 15. שמואל says this means 15 days after her טבילה. Since she has 7 days of נדה before she immerses, that is 22 days after her sighting.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this about
Immersion in a מקוה
A sighting of blood
A woman's regular, expected day of bleeding

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא אֶלָּא חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר לִטְבִילָתָהּ,
phrases.english: They taught this only about fifteen days from her immersion,
which are twenty-two days from her sighting,
phrases.notes: Add her 7 days of נדה before immersing: 7 + 15 = 22.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the explanation of the משנה that רב פפא's proof relies on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's numbers are counted from her טבילה, so 'day 15' means day 22 from her sighting.

steps.title: רב פפא's proof: her old day falls in her ימי זיבה, yet it is still forbidden
steps.stepSummary: She shifted to day 27, so her next 'day 22' falls in her ימי זיבה. The משנה still forbids it, which shows we worry about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: She shifted to day 27. So when 22 days come around again, she is in her ימי זיבה. Yet the משנה says both days are forbidden. This shows we do worry about her old day.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא does the math and draws his proof. Even though her old day now lands in her ימי זיבה, the משנה still says to be careful on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her new sighting on day 27 starts 7 days of נדה (27–33) and then 11 days of זיבה (34–44). Counting another 22 days from her old day 22 brings us to day 44, which is inside her ימי זיבה. The משנה says 'both are forbidden', so it worries about a וסת that falls in ימי זיבה.

keyTerms.meaning: She changed (shifted) her pattern
The 11 days after the 7 days of נדה
Both days are forbidden
Evidently / this shows that
We are concerned

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two counts. 'Day 20' in the משנה (from טבילה) is the same as day 27 from her sighting.

phrases.english: and she shifted to day twenty-seven;
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's 'day 20' after immersion: 7 + 20 = 27.

phrases.english: so that when twenty-two days come around again,
she stands within her days of ziva,
and the Mishnah teaches: both this and that are forbidden,
evidently we are concerned about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses שמואל's counting to show that the old day falls in ימי זיבה.
steps.raayaObject: That we worry about a woman's usual day even when it falls in her ימי זיבה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling 'זה וזה אסורין', read according to שמואל's counting.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the heart of רב פפא's proof. The rest of the section tests whether his math holds up.

steps.title: How רב פפא is counting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רב פפא's assumption: the 22-day count runs from her old day 22, but her days of נדה start from day 27.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא holds that we count the 22 days from her old day 22, but we count the start of her נדה period from day 27.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the hidden assumption behind רב פפא's proof. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate counts here. Her וסת of 22 days keeps running from the old day 22. Her נדה and זיבה days start from the actual sighting on day 27. Only with this mix does the next 'day 22' land in ימי זיבה.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds / his assumption is
We count
The נדה period and its opening (the start of the cycle)

phrases.english: And Rav Pappa holds:
the twenty-two days, we count from day twenty-two;
the niddah period and its start, we count from day twenty-seven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the counting method behind the proof in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The וסת count runs from the old day 22, while the נדה and זיבה days run from the new sighting on day 27.

steps.title: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע challenges the counting: maybe it lands in her ימי נדה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע asks: maybe the 22 days are also counted from day 27. Then the day lands in her ימי נדה, and there is no proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said to רב פפא: How do you know? Maybe the 22 days are also counted from day 27. Then, when 22 days come around again, she is in her ימי נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא pushes back on רב פפא's math. He offers a different way to count that takes away the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both counts start from day 27, the next 'day 22' is day 49. Her new cycle starts on day 45 (27 + 7 + 11), so day 49 is inside her ימי נדה, not her ימי זיבה. In that case the משנה's 'both are forbidden' tells us nothing about ימי זיבה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know?
Perhaps
Her 7 days of נדה

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's proof depends on how you count. If the 22 days run from day 27, her day falls in ימי נדה, and the משנה gives no proof about ימי זיבה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said to Rav Pappa:
From where do you know?

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא עֶשְׂרִין וְתַרְתֵּין נָמֵי מֵעֶשְׂרִין וְשִׁבְעָה מָנֵינַן,
phrases.english: Perhaps the twenty-two are also counted from day twenty-seven,
so that when twenty-two days come around again,
phrases.notes: Counting from 27, that brings us to day 49, after her new cycle has already begun.

phrases.english: she stands within her days of niddah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרַב פָּפָּא מִמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the counting assumption explained in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב פפא's proof from the משנה. It does not reject the rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the 22-day count runs from the old day 22. If it runs from day 27, the day falls in ימי נדה, not ימי זיבה.

steps.title: The chicken proves we count from the latest sighting
steps.stepSummary: A chicken that broke its lay-skip routine restarts the pattern from its latest egg, not from its original schedule. So a woman's count also restarts from her actual sighting on day 27.
steps.simpleTranslation: This makes sense too. Otherwise, think of a chicken that lays one day and skips one day, lays one day and skips one day, and then skipped two days and laid on one day. When it goes back to its routine, does it follow the order counted from its latest egg, or its original schedule? It must follow the order counted from its latest egg.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע continues his argument from Step 4. He gives logical support for his idea that the 22 days are counted from day 27, when she actually saw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A chicken's pattern clearly restarts from its last egg. It does not go back to its old schedule as if the break never happened. The same logic applies to a woman whose cycle shifted: her new count runs from her real sighting, not from her old day 22.

keyTerms.meaning: It is logical / it makes sense
A hen / chicken
Lays (an egg)
Holds back (does not lay)
According to what is ahead of it (counting from the latest event)
As it was from the beginning (the original schedule)

phrases.english: And so too it is logical;
for if you do not say so,
this chicken
that lays one day and holds back one day,
and lays one day and holds back one day,

phrases.aramaic: וְכָבְשָׁה תְּרֵי יוֹמֵי וְרָמְיָא חַד יוֹמָא,
phrases.english: and then held back two days and laid on one day,
when it goes back and takes up its routine,
does it take it up by the order ahead of it,
phrases.notes: Meaning it counts from its latest egg, so the next day would be a skip day.

phrases.english: or does it take it up as at the beginning?
Necessarily, it takes it up by the order ahead of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the דחיה of Step 4 with a logical comparison.
steps.raayaObject: That a shifted cycle is counted from the actual new sighting (day 27).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The everyday pattern of a chicken that restarts its lay-skip routine from its latest egg.
steps.whatToRemember: A pattern that gets interrupted restarts from the latest real event, not from the old schedule.

steps.title: רב פפא brings up the debate on fixing a cycle during ימי נדה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא quotes the מחלוקת: ריש לקיש says a woman fixes a וסת during ימי זיבה but not during ימי נדה, and רבי יוחנן says she does fix one during ימי נדה. Then he asks what case they are arguing about.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to him: But what about what ריש לקיש said: A woman fixes a cycle for herself during her days of זיבה, but she does not fix a cycle during her days of נדה. And רבי יוחנן says: A woman fixes a cycle during her days of נדה. What is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא begins pushing back on the idea from the chicken proof. He sets up the challenge by quoting a מחלוקת and asking what case it is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא signals that something becomes hard to explain if we accept the idea we just proved. רב פפא does not state the problem yet. He first needs to define the exact case of the מחלוקת, which happens in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: But then (signals that the new idea causes a problem)
Fixes a regular cycle (usually after three matching sightings)
The 11 days after her 7 days of נדה
The 7 days that start from her period
What is the case? / What are the circumstances?

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to him:
But that which Reish Lakish said:
A woman fixes a cycle for herself
during her days of ziva,
but a woman does not fix a cycle for herself
during her days of menstruation.
And Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
A woman fixes a cycle for herself
during her days of menstruation
what is the case?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא: אֶלָּא הָא דְּאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a challenge against the counting idea supported in Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the count restarts from her actual sighting.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב פפא will show that the case behind the ריש לקיש / רבי יוחנן מחלוקת does not fit this idea. The full argument comes after this step.
steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not asking about the מחלוקת for its own sake. He is using it as a tool to attack the idea that was just proven.

steps.title: Defining the case: sightings on the 1st and the 5th
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא suggests the case. She saw on the 1st and the 5th of one month, again on the 1st and the 5th of the next month, and now on the 5th only, not on the 1st.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not a case where she saw on the first of the month and on the fifth of the month, and on the first of the month and on the fifth of the month, and now she saw on the fifth of the month but did not see on the first of the month?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers his own question by describing the case of the מחלוקת. He is still building his challenge, and its punchline comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now she has three sightings on the 5th. The first two came only a few days after a sighting on the 1st, so they fell inside her ימי נדה. The third came with no sighting on the 1st before it. This is exactly the kind of case where it matters how we measure her ימי נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not? (introduces a suggested answer)
The beginning (first day) of the month
The fifth day of the month
Now (in the third month)

phrases.english: Is it not a case where she saw on the first of the month,
and on the fifth of the month,
and on the first of the month, and on the fifth of the month,
and now she saw on the fifth of the month,
but on the first of the month she did not see,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the היכי דמי of Step 6 by describing the case, as part of רב פפא's challenge.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is three sightings on the 5th of the month. The first two came right after sightings on the 1st, and the third came without one.
steps.whyThisMatters: This case will be the testing ground for whether ימי נדה are counted from the actual sighting, which is the idea under attack.

steps.title: רב פפא's conclusion: we count from the start of the month
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that his case is what רבי יוחנן was talking about when he ruled that a woman fixes a וסת during her ימי נדה. That shows we count from ראש חודש, her usual day, even though she did not see that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about this case רבי יוחנן says: a woman fixes a cycle for herself during her days of נדה. So clearly we count from the start of the month!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא finishes his proof. In the case he set up in step 7, the sighting on the 5th only counts as 'inside ימי נדה' if we count from ראש חודש, a day she did not actually see.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we counted from when she actually saw, the 5th would not be inside any ימי נדה at all. רבי יוחנן still calls it a sighting during ימי נדה, so the count must start from her usual date, ראש חודש. By the same logic, the 22-day count should run from her old usual day, not from day 27. That backs רב פפא's assumption from step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: Fixes a set menstrual pattern (a cycle she can rely on)
Her days of נדה, the 7 days that start from her period
Evidently / so we see that
The first of the month (ראש חודש)
We count

steps.confusionAlert: In this case she did NOT see on ראש חודש the third time. רב פפא's whole point is that we still count her ימי נדה from that day, because it is her usual day.

phrases.english: And about this he says:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יוחנן, and 'this' is the case רב פפא just described: the 1st and 5th, twice, then the 5th alone.

phrases.english: A woman fixes a cycle for herself
during her days of niddah,
evidently, we count from the start of the month!
phrases.notes: The 5th is only 'inside her ימי נדה' if we start counting from ראש חודש, even though she didn't see then.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָאָמַר: אִשָּׁה קוֹבַעַת לָהּ וֶסֶת בְּתוֹךְ יְמֵי נִדּוּתָהּ, אַלְמָא מֵרֵישׁ יַרְחָא מָנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof whose case was set up in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's assumption that the count runs from the woman's usual date and not from her actual later sighting.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a woman fixes a וסת during her ימי נדה, applied to the case of the 5th alone.

steps.title: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע gives a different case for רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says that is not רבי יוחנן's case. רבי יוחנן was talking about a woman who saw on the 1st, the 1st, the 25th, and then the 1st again. The last 1st falls inside the ימי נדה of the 25th. It still counts toward her וסת, because the 25th was just extra blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No. This is what רבי יוחנן said: for example, she saw on the first of the month, and on the first of the next month, and on the 25th of that month, and on the first of the following month. We say that the 25th was extra blood added in her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע rejects רב פפא's proof. He offers a different case for רבי יוחנן, one where every sighting really happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the new case, the last sighting on the 1st really is within 7 days of an actual sighting, the one on the 25th. So it truly is during ימי נדה, with no need to count from a day she didn't see. It still fixes her ראש חודש וסת, because the 25th is treated as a one-time extra flow that does not break her pattern. So רבי יוחנן's ruling says nothing about counting from a skipped usual date, and רב פפא's proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: For example / such as the case where
The 25th of the month
Extra blood, an additional flow outside her pattern
Were added / built up

steps.whyThisMatters: This fits רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's position from step 4. A count runs from the actual sighting, so רבי יוחנן's case must be one where the ימי נדה come from a real sighting.

phrases.english: He said to him: No,
this is what Rabbi Yochanan said:
for example, where she saw on the first of the month,
and on the first of the next month,
and on the twenty-fifth of that month,
and on the first of the following month,
phrases.notes: This last 1st comes only a few days after the 25th, so it falls inside the ימי נדה that began with that sighting.

phrases.english: where we say
it is extra blood that was added in her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 8's proof by explaining רבי יוחנן's case another way.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from רבי יוחנן. רבי יוחנן's ruling itself stays in place.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב פפא assumed רבי יוחנן's case needed counting from a skipped date. But רבי יוחנן's case can be one where the ימי נדה come from a real sighting on the 25th.

steps.title: רבין and the נחותי ימא support רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע
steps.stepSummary: When רבין and the other scholars who traveled from ארץ ישראל to בבל came, they reported רבי יוחנן's statement the way רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע explained it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise, when רבין and all the sea-travelers came, they said it like רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings outside support. The scholars who brought רבי יוחנן's teachings to בבל reported them the way רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע explained them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the argument between רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע. The case of רבי יוחנן is the 1st, 1st, 25th, 1st case. That means רב פפא's proof does not stand.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise
Sea-travelers, scholars who went between ארץ ישראל and בבל carrying teachings

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's ruling (a woman fixes a וסת during her ימי נדה) is about a real sighting inside ימי נדה, the 1st right after the 25th. It does not prove that we count from a usual day she skipped.

phrases.english: And likewise, when Ravin came
and all the sea-travelers,
phrases.notes: These are the scholars who traveled from ארץ ישראל to בבל and brought רבי יוחנן's teachings with them.

phrases.aramaic: אַמְרוּהָ כְּרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.
phrases.english: they said it in line with Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין וְכֹל נָחוֹתֵי יַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms step 9's reading of רבי יוחנן through reliable report.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן's case is as רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע explained it. So רב פפא's proof that the count runs from the usual date is rejected.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter of בנות כותים
steps.stepSummary: The closing line marks the end of the פרק בנות כותים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, בנות כותים.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional closing line at the end of a פרק. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן marks that the chapter is finished. It expresses the hope to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, the closing formula of a פרק
The name of this פרק, taken from its opening words

phrases.english: We will return to you, Benos Kusim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the sugya ends.
